info.description: Current implemented HTTP contract of the Hahn client and Rust server. Change it together with implementation and synthetic-data tests. The decisions behind it are in docs/adr/; no stable compatibility guarantee is made yet.
info.title: Hahn API

get.description: List of runs. Implement this as a light operation that does not open recordings.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Returns only runs whose name contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most runs to return. Values out of range or not numeric return 400.

get.description: A run and its groups. Implement this as a light operation that does not open recordings.
Time range and message count of a group. A group with no messages is a successful result without a time range.

History of messages or of a field, as a stream. Each request reads one field; read several fields of a topic with separate requests. Rows are not necessarily in primary-time order, since some recordings invert it, so a client that needs order sorts stably. Messages with the same time are separate rows.

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: `true` returns values for display. `false` returns exact values, without shortening strings, for where they are needed, such as plots: `path` must then name a single number, bool, enum or string field, anything else returning 422, and enums are returned as their name.

get.description: The latest message at or before `time_ns`, or `null` if the topic has no message by then.

The messages of a topic within a range of primary time, each converted to a frame of a Hahn type. Frames are in recording order, which is not necessarily primary-time order, since some recordings invert it. A client that needs time order, to connect a trajectory for example, sorts stably by `time_ns`, which keeps frames with the same time in recording order.

The current message at `time_ns`, converted to a Hahn type: at most one frame followed by `complete`, and just `complete` with no message by then. The current message is the latest one at or before that time. Among messages with the same time, it is the last in recording order, so one recording always gives one answer. An old message stays current until the next one; the protocol has no way yet to say that a value has gone.

parameters.name: known_time_ns
parameters.description: The `time_ns` of the frame this operation last returned, to avoid resending a value that has not changed: when the current message has that time, the response has `{"type":"unchanged"}` in place of the frame. Do not pass a time taken from `/views`: messages with the same time are separate frames there, and the client may hold one that is not the current one.

get.description: The coordinate frames of a run.
The transforms of the run's static frames, which hold at all times. The client resolves frames from these and the dynamic samples.
The samples of the run's dynamic frames recorded in a range of recording time. Request a margin beyond what is shown: measurement stamps lag recording time.

parameters.name: start_ns
parameters.description: Inclusive start of the recording-time range.

parameters.name: end_ns
parameters.description: Exclusive end of the recording-time range.

Id.description: A URL-safe id of a run or group. Dots are not allowed, because URL parsers treat `.` and `..` as path segments; a server deriving ids from file names replaces them. A client uses it as it is in URLs, and its content has no meaning.

TimeNs.description: Unsigned nanoseconds as a decimal string because JavaScript numbers lack the precision. The current API uses the recording time (MCAP log_time); it may be relative rather than a Unix epoch timestamp.

Count.description: A count, as a JSON number within the safe integer range.

ErrorCode.description: Identifies the failure; clients branch on it and never parse the description. Treat a code you do not know as a failure of unknown kind, never as an empty result. The README lists what each code means.

Quaternion.description: A rotation as `[x, y, z, w]`, of unit length: a server normalizes them, and treats a recorded one of zero length, such as an unset rotation, as no rotation.

Pose.description: A position and orientation, moving a point into the parent: `p_parent = orientation * p + position`.

Transform.description: Moves a point into the target: `p_target = rotation * p_frame + translation`.

BlobRef.description: A range of the payload of a frame

offset.description: Bytes from the start of the payload. Always a multiple of 8.

length.description: Size of the data in bytes, without the padding after it.

FrameId.description: The coordinate frame of the coordinates: an `id` in `/frames`, unless the run has no transforms for it, or `null` when unknown.

items.description: The server decides the order. Clients only see the head of the list, so returning recent or relevant runs first is recommended.

truncated.description: `true` when more runs match than `limit` allows. There is no paging; narrow the search instead.

groups.description: The client shows a run with no groups as an error.

timezone.description: The timezone of where the run took place: an IANA name such as `Asia/Tokyo`, or `null` when unknown. A display hint for the client; times always stay in UTC.

default_open.description: Whether to open the group first when opening the run. It is fine for no group to be `true`; the user then chooses which groups to open. The client opens the only group of a run regardless.

end_ns.description: The last primary time. Unlike a range in a request, it includes the last time. Omitted, like `start_ns`, when the group has no messages.

message_count.description: `null` when the recording has no statistics.

start_ns.description: The first primary time. Omitted, like `end_ns`, when the group has no messages.

id.description: Opaque identifier unique within the group. Use as the topic parameter in requests.

error.description: Why the topic cannot be decoded. Such a topic is still listed, with empty `fields`.

fields.description: The fields of a message, as a tree.

schema_encoding.description: Lets a client name types in the schema's own language, such as ROS 2 or protobuf.

schema_name.description: The name of the user type.

topic.description: Topic name for display; multiple items may share the same name.

meta_fields.description: Values recorded separately from the message rather than inside it, in the same shape as `fields`. For MCAP it has `log_time` and `publish_time`. The server decides which exist, and it is empty if there are none.

views.description: The views the topic offers, empty when it cannot be converted. The server decides from the schema, without reading messages.

name.description: Names starting with `$` are reserved, to tell them apart from `$truncated` and `$bytes` in values. Servers must not return them: if a recording contains one, either report an error for that topic or recording, or return the field under another name.

data_type.description: The kind of value, which decides how a client reads it. Details such as bounds belong in `type_name`.

enum_values.description: The ordered names and values of an enum. Values hold the number; the name shown for it is the first entry with that value.

element.description: The element type of a list or array. Structs inside lists are described here too. Maps have no element schema.

value.description: A decimal string, like other 64-bit integers.

View.description: A conversion of a topic to a Hahn type.

id.description: Unique within the topic, and its content has no meaning. Requests name a view by `id`, since a topic can offer several views, even of one Hahn type.

kind.description: The Hahn type. A client ignores a view whose `kind` it does not know.

calibration.description: For an image: the calibration view of the same camera that topic names suggest, such as `/cam/camera_info` for `/cam/image_raw`, or `/cam/calibration` for `/cam`. Omitted when none or several are found. A suggestion: the client lets the user choose another.

topic.description: A topic `id` in the same group.

rectified.description: For an image: whether its pixels are rectified, when its topic name says so (`rect` or `raw`). Omitted when unknown; a client then treats them as raw.

MessagesEvent.description: One line of a message stream

scanned_messages.description: The running total read by this request, which is not progress through the whole recording.

value.description: The message or field, in the form described under Message values in the README.

scanned_messages.description: The total read by this request.

FrameList.description: The frames of a run. A run without transforms has an empty list.

unreadable_groups.description: IDs of the run's groups left out of the graph because they could not be read.

parent.description: The parent last recorded, or `null` for a frame that is only ever a parent. `parents` lists every one.

kind.description: Whether the frame's transform to its parent holds at all times or changes with time. Omitted for a frame that is only ever a parent. A frame on both static and dynamic topics is dynamic.

parents.description: Every parent recorded for the frame, in the order first recorded.

dropped_samples.description: Samples of this frame left out because they hold a number that is not finite or no parent.

StaticTransform.description: A transform that holds at all times: `p_parent = rotation * p_child + translation`.

transforms.description: One per static frame, the last recorded, sorted by `child`.

DynamicTransform.description: One recorded sample of a changing transform.

stamp_ns.description: When the transform was measured, such as its `header.stamp`. Omitted when unknown or zero; never replaced by recording time.

samples.description: In recording order: by `time_ns`, then the order read. Samples are not merged: equal times stay separate rows.

ViewEvent.description: The JSON header of one frame

oneOf.description: A message that could not be converted. The stream goes on. The schema cannot rule out bad values.

error.description: Why it could not be converted.

oneOf.description: In place of a frame: the client already holds the value, as `known_time_ns` said.

ViewValue.description: A value of a Hahn type. The rules common to all of them are in the README.

FramedValue.description: Coordinate frame and measurement time of a spatial value.

stamp_ns.description: When the value was measured, such as the message's `header.stamp`, on the recording's measurement clock. Omitted when the message has no stamp or a zero one; the frame's `time_ns`, which is recording time, is never a substitute.

ImageValue.description: An encoded image or raw pixel image.

format.description: Image file encoding, or raw for pixel data. jpg is normalized to jpeg.

data.description: Blob of image file bytes, or raw pixel bytes when format is raw.

role.description: The current converter emits color images.

step.description: Raw image row stride in bytes.

encoding.description: Pixel encoding for a raw image.

PointCloudValue.description: A point cloud, with one blob per column so that a client can use them as typed arrays directly. Laser scans are converted to these. A server drops points without a position, and may send fewer points or fields than were recorded, to save transfer.

pose.description: The origin of the points in `frame_id`: `p_frame = orientation * p_point + position`.

positions.description: Blob of f32 `[x, y, z]` for each of the `count` points, in meters, all finite. Positions are f32, so a server moves large coordinates into `pose`.

fields.description: Further values per point, such as `intensity`. Empty when there are none.

data.description: Blob of one value per point.

omitted.description: Points left out because their position was not finite.

GeoLocationValue.description: One location on the earth, WGS 84, such as a GNSS fix. A single value: a client may draw a topic's history of them as a trail.

altitude.description: Meters above the WGS 84 ellipsoid, when known.

heading.description: Radians clockwise from true north, when known.

accuracy_m.description: Horizontal standard deviation in meters, when known.

stamp_ns.description: When the value was measured, such as the message's `header.stamp`, on the recording's measurement clock. Omitted when the message has no stamp or a zero one; the frame's `time_ns`, which is recording time, is never a substitute.

GeoValue.description: Shapes on a map, all held by one message, such as foxglove.GeoJSON. Each message replaces them entirely, and they are never joined across messages. A single location is a `geo_location`.

geometry.description: Any GeoJSON geometry, with positions as `[longitude, latitude]` in degrees, WGS 84.

properties.description: Free for the server to fill. A client may show it.

stamp_ns.description: When the value was measured, such as the message's `header.stamp`, on the recording's measurement clock. Omitted when the message has no stamp or a zero one; the frame's `time_ns`, which is recording time, is never a substitute.

omitted.description: Features left out because their geometry was missing or off the earth.

CameraCalibrationValue.description: Pinhole camera calibration. Image coordinates have x right and y down; the optical axis is positive z.

distortion.description: Distortion coefficients; an empty or all-zero array means no distortion.

distortion_model.description: Name of the distortion model, such as plumb_bob.

stamp_ns.description: When the value was measured, such as the message's `header.stamp`, on the recording's measurement clock. Omitted when the message has no stamp or a zero one; the frame's `time_ns`, which is recording time, is never a substitute.

projection.description: Row-major 3 by 4 projection matrix P, for rectified images, which take it without distortion. Omitted when not recorded or unusable.

PoseValue.description: A position and orientation in frame_id.

PositionValue.description: One position in frame_id, without an orientation. A single value: its history may be drawn as a trail.

PosesValue.description: Poses in frame_id without an order, such as particles. One message holds them all and replaces the last; they are never joined to each other or across messages.

omitted.description: Poses left out because they were not finite or could not be read.

PathValue.description: Poses in frame_id in order, such as a planned route, drawn joined. One message holds the whole path and replaces the last. A pose that is not finite fails the message.

Bbox3dValue.description: Boxes in frame_id, such as detected objects, all held by one message, which replaces the last. Boxes are never joined across messages, even by `id`.

size.description: Full size in meters along the box's own x, y and z.

label.description: What it is, such as a class name.

score.description: How sure the detector is, usually 0 to 1.

id.description: Which object it is, as a tracker names it.

omitted.description: Boxes left out because they were not finite, had a negative size or could not be read.

ImageAnnotationsValue.description: Marks over one image, in its pixels, all held by one message, which replaces the last. Which image they mark is not in the value: neither `frame_id` nor topic names establish it, so the user chooses which topics an image shows. A client shows a message's marks over the image with the same `stamp_ns`, or, without stamps, over images recorded at or after them.

stamp_ns.description: When the value was measured, such as the message's `header.stamp`, on the recording's measurement clock. Omitted when the message has no stamp or a zero one; the frame's `time_ns`, which is recording time, is never a substitute.

type.description: `points`; `line_strip`, joined in order; `line_loop`, closed, as for a box; `line_list`, separate pairs; `circle`; or `text`. A client skips a type it does not know.

items.description: `[x, y]` in pixels from the image's top left.

position.description: The center of a circle, or where a text starts.

label.description: What it marks, such as a class name.

score.description: How sure the detector is, usually 0 to 1.

id.description: Which object it marks, as a tracker names it.

omitted.description: Annotations left out because a number in them was not finite or they could not be read.

Topic.name: topic
Topic.description: The topic ID returned in the group topic list.

ViewId.name: view
ViewId.description: The `id` of a view of the topic.

FieldPath.name: path
FieldPath.description: The field to read, as a JSON array of field names in a string, for example `["pose","x"]`, so that names containing dots stay unambiguous. Without it, the whole topic.

Meta.name: meta
Meta.description: Reads a `meta_fields` value, for example `publish_time`, instead of `path`. The two cannot be combined (400). These values are kept apart from the message, so they are not part of the whole topic's value. They are 64-bit integers, so they are returned as strings.

StartNs.name: start_ns
StartNs.description: The start of the range in primary time, included. Greater than `end_ns` returns 400.

EndNs.name: end_ns
EndNs.description: The end of the range in primary time, excluded. To read through the last time, omit it.

ViewFrames.description: Binary frames; the schema is the header of one
